/-!
# Conjecture 8.8

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Part b) of the problem, due to D. V. Anosov, asks:

Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ which contains an
element $a$ such that each element of $G$ is conjugate to some power of $a$?

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a quotient of a free group
on finitely many generators by the normal closure of finitely many relators.
Mathlib has `PresentedGroup` but no predicate for finite presentability, so it is
defined in this file.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by a
finite presentation $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$, i.e. the
quotient of the free group on $n$ generators by the normal closure of a finite set of
relators.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Group.FG (too weak: finitely generated only), PresentedGroup (construction, not a predicate; used as the building block), Algebra.FinitePresentation / Module.FinitePresentation (ring/module-theoretic, not applicable to groups).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.8».IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: The problem requires G to be finitely presented. Mathlib only has Group.FG (finitely generated, strictly weaker) and PresentedGroup (a construction, not a predicate), and FormalConjecturesForMathlib has nothing on group presentations. Defined as ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))), Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set _) ≃* G), i.e. isomorphic to a free group on finitely many generators modulo the normal closure of finitely many relators. Three short @[category API] lemmas test it (presented groups on finite data are finitely presented; invariance under MulEquiv; finitely presented implies Group.FG).

blocks.name: IsFinitelyPresented
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by a
finite presentation $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$, i.e. the
quotient of the free group on $n$ generators by the normal closure of a finite set of
relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H]
    (e : G ≃* H) (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : IsFinitelyPresented H := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨f⟩⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨n, rels, ⟨f.trans e⟩⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := hG
  haveI : Group.FG (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of _,
      Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence Prop (∃ G finitely presented, ¬IsCyclic G, ∃ a, ∀ g, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n)); 'power' should be read as an integer power, and Mathlib has Group.FG but no ready-made 'finitely presented group' predicate, so finite presentability (a finite generating set together with a finitely normally generated relation subgroup of the free group) must be defined explicitly rather than weakened to finitely generated.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical, faithful main theorem: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ IsCyclic G ∧ ∃ a, ∀ g, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n). Quantifier order matches the source, 'power' is an integer power per the notes, Mathlib's IsCyclic makes the trivial group and ℤ cyclic (so degenerate witnesses are excluded), and finite presentability is defined explicitly via PresentedGroup over Fin n with a Finset of relators rather than weakened to Group.FG. c04 was chosen because CONTRIBUTING.md asks for basic API tests for bespoke definitions and c04 supplies the most complete set (PresentedGroup instance, isomorphism invariance, finitely-generated consequence), all proven and compiling warning-free. Only edit: docstring sentence explaining the ¬ IsCyclic reading.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.8

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Part b) of the problem, due to D. V. Anosov, asks:

Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ which contains an
element $a$ such that each element of $G$ is conjugate to some power of $a$?

A group is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a quotient of a free group
on finitely many generators by the normal closure of finitely many relators.
Mathlib has `PresentedGroup` but no predicate for finite presentability, so it is
defined in this file.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.8»

/-- A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group given by a
finite presentation $\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$, i.e. the
quotient of the free group on $n$ generators by the normal closure of a finite set of
relators. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
    Nonempty (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) ≃* G)

/-- A group given by a finite presentation is finitely presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
  ⟨n, rels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- Finite presentability is invariant under group isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H]
    (e : G ≃* H) (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : IsFinitelyPresented H := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨f⟩⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨n, rels, ⟨f.trans e⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
lemma IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) : Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨n, rels, ⟨e⟩⟩ := hG
  haveI : Group.FG (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of _,
      Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

/--
(D. V. Anosov) Does there exist a non-cyclic finitely presented group $G$ which
contains an element $a$ such that each element of $G$ is conjugate to some power
of $a$?

Here "power" means an integer power $a^n$ with $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, and "non-cyclic"
is `¬ IsCyclic G`, which excludes the trivial group and the infinite cyclic group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.8».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ¬ IsCyclic G ∧
      ∃ a : G, ∀ g : G, ∃ n : ℤ, IsConj g (a ^ n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.8»

items: 'Power of a' read as integer power a ^ (n : ℤ), as the decomposition notes require (a^{-1} etc. included).

'Non-cyclic' formalized as ¬ IsCyclic G using Mathlib's IsCyclic, which counts the trivial group and infinite cyclic groups as cyclic; this excludes exactly the groups where the property holds trivially (every element is a power of a generator).
The group G is quantified over Type (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files; no generality is lost since finitely presented groups are countable and the property is isomorphism-invariant.

IsFinitelyPresented is stated existentially (some finite presentation exists) via isomorphism to PresentedGroup over FreeGroup (Fin n) with a Finset of relators; this is the standard definition and is equivalent to the 'every finite generating set has finitely many defining relations' formulation.

IsConj g (a ^ n) is used; IsConj is symmetric, so the direction is immaterial. The definition is placed in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) rather than FormalConjecturesForMathlib, because the sandbox only permits writing the candidate file; a reviewer may prefer to move it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted the slot; all reports were 'formalized_with_new_definitions' and all compiled. Definitions across candidates are equivalent variants (isomorphism to PresentedGroup in either direction; c02 uses surjection with kernel = normal closure of a finite set; c03 uses arbitrary finite generator type and Set.Finite relators). The bespoke IsFinitelyPresented lives in the problem file (as with IsTarskiMonster in Kourovka/1_74.lean); a maintainer may prefer moving it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/GroupTheory/ as a reusable definition. The witness group is quantified over Type (universe 0), following Kourovka idiom; this loses nothing since finitely presented groups are countable and the property is isomorphism-invariant. Final file compiles with `lake env lean --json` reporting only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
